sentences.text: Palle Suman, vs The High Court Of Telangana on 10 April, 2025

Author: N. Tukaramji
Bench: N. Tukaramji
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice N. Tukaramji
 Criminal Petition No.4948 of 2025
Order:

This petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS, 2023') seeking quashment of the proceedings in Crime No.81 of 2025 for the offence under Section 69 of BNS Act pending on the file of the Deverakonda Police Station, against the petitioner/accused.

[
2. Heard Mr.Rapolu Bhaskar, learned counsel for petitioner- accused, Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.

3. The petitioner/sole accused is facing accusation under Section 69 of BNS Act, in Crime No.81 of 2025 on the file of the Deverakonda Police Station,
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that even a bare reading of the complaint is not disclosing any offence.

In any case, the referred incident is of the year 2019 and after seven years,
the complaint has been lodged and it is making out the falsity beyond the period of limitation.
The Hon'ble Supreme court in Biswajyoti NTR,J Chatterjee vs. State of West Bengal 1, considering the facts quashed the proceedings.

entities.text: Biswajyoti NTR,J Chatterjee vs. State of West Bengal 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus prayed for interference.
5. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that there are specific allegations against the petitioner and as on the date the petitioner is absconding and the investigation is in progress.
6. I have perused the materials placed on record.
7. The allegations in the police report are clearly against the petitioner with reference of first occurrence on March, 2019.
Nonetheless, the substance is making out that the de facto complaint has been sexually exploited under the promise of marriage and the accused continued to do so even after his employment.

These averments are making out that though the first occurrence was of 2019,
as continuous exploitation has been mentioned, drawing a conclusion that for the seven years old incident, the complaint has been lodged, would not be proper.

Palle Suman, vs The High Court Of Telangana on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72497519/
1 8.

entities.text: Palle Suman, vs The High Court Of Telangana on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, the authority cited by the petitioner is in respect of prosecution under Sections 376, 417,
506 of IPC, whereas, the present complaint has been registered under Section 69 of BNS, which prescribes that sexual exploitation under the promise of 2025 SCC Online SC 741 NTR,J marriage is an offence.
Thus, the authority is distinguishable in facts and law.

9. That being the position and as there is prima facie case and the investigation is at preliminary stage and particularly the petitioners conduct of avoiding the judicial process, this Court finds no tenable ground for interfere with the proceedings.
10. For the aforesaid reasons, no merit is found in the petition and in effect, this petition is liable to be and is accordingly dismissed.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE N. TUKARAMJI Date: 10.04.2025 mmr NTR,J THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE N. TUKARAMJI CRIMINAL PETITION No.4948 of 2025 DATE:
